rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance - Rent Increase Limit
rules.requirement: Residential rent increases are limited to the lower of 3% per year or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.
rules.key_value: lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index
rules.exemptions: The rent cap does not apply to residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995. [Rent Stabilization Ordinance, Rent Cap Exemptions]; The rent cap does not apply to mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990. [Rent Stabilization Ordinance, Rent Cap Exemptions]
rules.citation: Rent Stabilization Ordinance, Rent Increase Limit
rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.

rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance - Fair Return Petition
rules.requirement: An owner of residential rental property or a mobile home park may petition for relief from the rent cap by providing evidence that an increase in excess of the annual allowance is necessary to provide a fair and reasonable return. The City Manager or designee will decide on the petition within 60 days of receiving a complete application.
rules.citation: Rent Stabilization Ordinance, Fair Return Petition
rules.quoted_span: Any owner of residential rental property or a mobile home park may petition for relief from the cap, but will need to provide evidence that a rate increase in excess of the annual allowance is necessary to provide a fair and reasonable return for their property. The City Manager, or designee, may consider a variety of relevant factors and will decide on the petition within 60 days of receiving a complete application.

rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance - Written Notice to Tenants
rules.requirement: Property owners must provide written notice of the Rent Stabilization Ordinance and tenant's rights at the commencement of a lease or as part of any notice to increase rent.
rules.quoted_span: Property owners are required to provide written notice of the Ordinance and tenant’s rights at commencement of a lease or as part of any notice to increase rent.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - Just Cause Required
rules.requirement: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which must be stated in a written notice.
rules.citation: Just Cause Eviction Ordinance, Just Cause Requirement
rules.quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - Notice of Violation and Opportunity to Cure
rules.requirement: Before issuing a notice to terminate for just cause, the owner must first give notice of the violation with a time period for the tenant to fix the violation.
rules.citation: Just Cause Eviction Ordinance, Notice of Violation
rules.quoted_span: Before issuing a notice to terminate for just cause, the owner shall first give notice of the violation with a time period for the tenant to fix the violation(s).

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - Relocation Assistance or Rent Waiver
rules.requirement: Under a no-fault just cause termination, the owner must either provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive payment of rent for the final 3 months of the tenancy.
rules.coverage_conditions: Under a no-fault just cause termination
rules.citation: Just Cause Eviction Ordinance, Relocation Assistance
rules.quoted_span: Under a no-fault just cause termination, the owner shall either provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive payment of rent for the final 3 months of the tenancy.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - Written Notice to Tenants
rules.requirement: Property owners must provide notice of the Just Cause Eviction Ordinance protections to existing tenants before December 19, 2021, or at the commencement or renewal of their lease.
rules.citation: Just Cause Eviction Ordinance, Notice Requirements
rules.quoted_span: Property owners must provide notice to existing tenants before December 19, 2021, or at commencement or renewal of their lease of the Just Cause Eviction Ordinance protections.

provisions.summary: Limits residential rent increases to the lower of 3% per year or 80% of CPI change, and prohibits increases if CPI is negative.
Permits owners of residential rental property or mobile home parks to petition for relief from the rent cap for a fair and reasonable return.
Requires property owners to provide written notice of the ordinance and tenant rights at lease commencement or with any rent increase notice.
Prohibits terminating a tenancy after 30 days without just cause stated in a written notice.
Requires notice of violation and a cure period before issuing a notice to terminate for just cause.
Requires 3 months of relocation assistance or waiver of the final 3 months of rent for no-fault just cause terminations.
Requires property owners to notify existing tenants before December 19, 2021, or at lease commencement or renewal, of Just Cause protections.
